blog_summary: Adrian Colyer highlights Pregelix as an innovative approach that combines the strengths of in-memory graph processing (like FlashGraph) with dataflow engines (like GraphX). The paper demonstrates how to implement the Pregel programming model using a set-oriented iterative dataflow approach, leveraging relational operators such as joins and group-bys to model message passing. This allows Pregelix to run on existing shared-nothing dataflow engines like Hyracks, benefiting from their out-of-core support and query optimization capabilities. Colyer emphasizes the flexibility of Pregelix, which offers multiple physical execution strategies (16 tailored options) for different workloads, and its reduced code complexity compared to specialized graph engines like Giraph. The paper also underscores the broader insight that declarative, logic-based approaches (e.g., Datalog) can parallelize recursive computations efficiently, a lesson that has been underutilized in systems like MapReduce.
paper_title: Pregelix: Big(ger) Graph Analytics on a Dataflow Engine
